summary.intent: Resolve open Entire review findings on the caliper PR stack, find the recurring patterns behind them, and assess whether architecture, models, and traits need adjusting across all changes since 0.11.0.
summary.outcome: Pushed the f29013d5 fix for Finding B on #469 and resolved it in Entire (Finding A stays open pending the user's decision). Categorized ~15 distinct open findings into 5 patterns and started workers on PR conflicts and the #475 exact-or-declined fix, plus a read-only architecture review.

repo: ADR 0026: the checker is the type authority and the structural lane is the fast path, so structural expansion should be exact or declined.
Stacked PRs duplicate findings: #469's collapse findings reappear on #475, #476, #477 and #478, so the raw count (~30) is about double the distinct count (~15).
The checker cannot distinguish Pick from Omit because the TS lib writes Omit as a Pick. Fixing the checker-only alias Pick case needs Omit/Pick provenance from tsrs.
The checker returns empty JSDoc for every prop (tsrs 0.24 getDocumentationComment), so checker-only sources get no description. The test the_checker_answers_a_props_jsdoc is #[ignore]d.

BodyFacts defaults to complete and becomes incomplete only when flagged, so a declared function with no body counts as a complete empty body. It should start unknown and become complete only after full classification.
The heap budget (#474) parses cgroup files with hard-coded v1 mount paths. A maintained cgroup crate is preferred over our own parser.
The finding_b_* test lives in crates/semantic/tests/collapse_model.rs and fails on the base commit.
Open PRs #477, #478, #479, #480 and #483 report CONFLICTING because they embed older copies of #469, #470 and main.

code.finding: Contains finding_b_* tests that fail on base and pass at f29013d5; line numbers were not given in the transcript.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output with no user authority. The assistant correctly reported the results and left the Finding A dismissal to the user.
Dismissing a finding needs the user's say-so, so Finding A was left open.
Worker cap is three concurrent workers. Work touching the same files (pattern 3 and the conflict merge) is serialized to avoid conflicts.
Merging stacked PRs in order (#469, #470, #474) is cheaper than keeping the stack alive and removes duplicate review findings.
Use `entire trail finding list/show/resolve` with --branch/--repo/--project flags to triage findings per change.

friction: Stacked PRs make reviewers see the same diff repeatedly, inflating finding counts.
Five PRs conflict with main and with older copies of #469 and #470.
The worker's memory figure was from the small chakra fixture, not the 6.4→1.9 GB corpus run, so it only shows no regression.
The worker did not update the #469 PR body.
The checker's lack of JSDoc and of Omit/Pick provenance limits fixes without upstream tsrs changes.
open_items: Finding A (checker-only alias Pick collapse) is awaiting the user's decision to accept the limit or request tsrs provenance upstream.
Named-alias Pick and checker JSDoc remain; file an upstream tsrs issue covering JSDoc and the slimmer getPropertiesOfType request.
Fold the reviewer's remaining items into the #469 PR body.
Merge f29013d5 and the #470 fix forward into #472, #475 and the wave-1 branches.
Pattern 3: make BodyFacts unknown by default and add a generated differential test (#470, #480).
Pattern 4: choose a maintained cgroup crate to replace the heap budget parser (#474).

Wait for the conflict-merge worker, the #475 exact-or-declined worker, the /code-review on wave1-base, and the architecture review at ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/architecture-review.md before starting refactors.
